correctness.rationale: Every pentagonal face forces at least one frustrated edge; 12 faces double count 30 edges, giving >=6 frustrated edges. At equality these edges are perfect matchings of 12-vertex icosahedral dual, and facial-cycle consistency gives precisely two spin lifts per matching. Exact face-dual enumeration proves 125 matchings, while independent enumeration of all 2^20 spin states yields precisely 250 ground states and their 20-by-20 correlation matrix. Exact Newton trace computations verify det(x I-250 C)=(x-8)(x-48)^5(x-72)^4(x-408)^4(x^2-944x+22784)^3. Roots are positive, and row sum 8 gives unique weakest uniform mode. Finite-temperature Gibbs differentiation and limit at zero field prove the Curie response statement. No extrapolation to arbitrary graphs.

originality.rationale: Compared source claims and implications, not title overlap. Existing 2015 dodecahedral enumeration fixes 250 configurations and uniform magnetization moments, 2025 Ising-limit work gives mean nearest-neighbor -3/5, and published 2026 studies cover a transverse-field dynamics problem or a different 60-site fullerene. None of the examined relevant text supplied the complete six-distance covariance and exact six-eigenvalue, full-rank C20 local-field response with sharp anisotropy 59+25sqrt(5). Full historical-priority certainty is not claimed, especially given partially accessible 2025 source and index limitations.

value.rationale: The zero-temperature local-field susceptibility is a natural physical observable not determined by known uniform magnetocaloric data. The proof provides all six inequivalent spatial correlations, complete exact rank-20 susceptibility spectrum and a surprising sharp 59+25sqrt(5) patterned-versus-uniform response anisotropy on the smallest fullerene. It distinguishes quantum-network spin response to spatially heterogeneous probes in a canonical frustrated geometry and supplies a reproducible finite-size benchmark, without unsupported infinite-volume claims.
